content.text:
Reference image 1 shows a bald eagle. Use it only for the head.
Reference image 2 shows a lion. Use it only for the torso, limbs, skin covering and tail.
Create one new creature with a single, committed quadruped body plan.
Place the bald eagle's head on the lion's frame so every join heals naturally: no visible seams, no floating parts, no duplicated limbs.
A fusion with a body_plan conflict (e.g. finned x quadruped with no amphibious design note) must be flagged, not silently resolved by picking one parent's plan.
Show the full body in a calm three-quarter view on a plain, softly lit background, in the style of a natural history field-guide plate. Photographic realism, accurate anatomy, no text, no labels, no people.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Composing eagle-lion fusion**
I'm assembling a single quadruped that uses the bald eagle's head on the lion's torso, limbs, and tail, healing the join naturally for a calm three-quarter view in natural-history field-guide style.
**Refining eagle-lion fusion**
I'm adjusting the composite to swap the lion's head for a bald eagle's white head and yellow beak, keeping the tan lion body, tail tuft, and four limbs in a three-quarter view with a softly lit, field-guide background.
